items.title: Shiv–Shakti: relationship and meaning
items.description: Explore the relationship of Shiva and Shakti through devotional interpretations. Different traditions give different philosophical emphasis.

items.title: Ardhanarishvara: a shared form
items.description: The composite form joins Shiva and Parvati. Study its symbolism and artistic variations without treating one interpretation as universal.

items.title: Names, texts and early worship
items.description: Separate textual traditions and the development of worship from an invented birth date or a single chronological life story.

items.title: Sati, Daksha and sacred geography
items.description: A cycle of stories about Sati and Daksha is linked in devotional traditions to the Shakti Peethas. Retell with care, without graphic detail.

items.title: Parvati, devotion and union
items.description: Explore Parvati’s devotion and her union with Shiva as told across narrative traditions, rather than as one fixed historical sequence.

items.title: Ganesha, Skanda and family stories
items.description: Meet the household stories associated with Shiva and Parvati. Versions of origin stories differ, and retellings should name their source.

items.title: Neelakantha and the ocean-churning story
items.description: The blue-throated form is associated with Shiva containing poison during the ocean-churning narrative. It is religious storytelling, not a real-world safety practice.

items.title: Gangadhara and the descent of Ganga
items.description: Follow narratives of the Ganges descending through Shiva’s locks, and distinguish devotional meaning from geographical explanation.

items.title: The crescent moon and sacred symbols
items.description: Read the crescent moon and other attributes as iconographic themes. Connect to the existing Nandi, Vasuki, Trishul and Damru content modules for further review.

items.title: Nataraja: dance, change and renewal
items.description: Explore Shiva’s dancing form through art and religious interpretation. Do not promise that a visual model reproduces a consecrated image or ritual.

items.title: Bhairava, Tripurari and the lingam
items.description: Introduce distinct forms and stories as separate study paths; avoid merging regional versions or calling symbolic accounts scientific events.

items.title: Temples, festivals and living traditions
items.description: Connect narratives with temple-specific histories, devotional communities and festival practices. Current timings and ritual rules need local verification.

items.title: Kamakhya
items.description: Kamakhya is identified as a Shakti Peetha on Nilachal Hills in the official tourism account. The source presents the Sati association as a religious legend, not an archaeological finding.

items.title: Kalighat
items.description: West Bengal Tourism describes the Kali shrine at Kalighat and its religious setting by the Adi Ganga. The source uses a 52-Peetha framing. Retain that distinction instead of forcing it into a universal list.

items.title: Tripura Sundari / Matabari
items.description: Tripura Tourism attributes construction of the Matabari temple to Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in 1501. The construction date is a source-attributed historical statement; the sacred-origin narrative is a separate layer. This is not the similarly named temple at Banswara.

items.title: Ambaji
items.description: Gujarat Tourism identifies Ambaji with Arasuri Amba and the surrounding Arasur/Gabbar landscape. Sacred-origin claims are attributed to local tradition. Exact antiquity and archaeological chronology need separate scrutiny.

items.title: Jwalamukhi / Jawala Mata
items.description: The temple administration describes worship associated with flames at the shrine. Its account links the shrine to Sati lore. Specific body-part wording varies even within the cited page; no definitive body-part assignment is stored.

items.title: Mahalakshmi / Ambabai
items.description: The official tourism overview includes Mahalakshmi in the regional three-and-a-half Shakti Peetha tradition. Temple history, local Kolhasur lore and architectural periods require separate attribution; no miracle or prosperity guarantee is offered.

items.title: Tulja Bhavani
items.description: Maharashtra Tourism identifies the Tuljapur temple as part of the regional three-and-a-half grouping. Regional devotional identity is preserved; it is not automatically assigned a slot in every pan-Indian list.

items.title: Renuka Devi
items.description: Nanded district describes Renuka Devi’s shrine at Mahur as an important Shaktipith of Maharashtra. The source uses qualified wording for its construction history. No exact founding year is invented here.

items.title: Saptashrungi
items.description: Nashik district explicitly describes Saptashrungi as an Ardha Shaktipeeth and connects its name with seven peaks. The half-Peetha classification belongs to the regional grouping; it is not a fractional product or agent count.

items.title: Devon Ke Dev… Mahadev
items.description: A separate television-context lane for the likely intended Mahadev serial. Compare adaptations with named narrative traditions rather than treating episodes as scripture or historical proof.

items.title: Seasonal fruit plate
items.description: A food-design concept; check the specific temple or household tradition before treating it as an offering.
steps: Wash hands, utensils and the fruit.
Peel or cut using clean equipment; adjust cuts for choking risks and individual needs.
Arrange a small portion on a clean plate.
Serve promptly and refrigerate cut-fruit leftovers promptly.

items.title: Coconut & roasted chana plate
items.description: Not universally prescribed for worship or fasting; this is an editorial food concept.
steps: Check ingredient labels and individual allergies, including coconut and chickpea sensitivity.
Use a clean surface and safely prepared coconut pieces.
Arrange with a modest portion of roasted chana; adapt texture for children or swallowing difficulties.
Serve hygienically; keep perishables chilled when not serving.

items.title: Plain yogurt & fruit bowl
items.description: Contains milk. No medical diet, fasting certification or universal ritual suitability is claimed.
steps: Keep the pasteurised yogurt refrigerated.
Wash and prepare fruit with clean utensils.
Combine a small portion shortly before serving.
Check dairy allergy and individual suitability; return leftovers promptly to refrigeration.

review_gates: Stories are editorial proposals; devotional traditions and interpretations vary.
The Peetha list is a source-attributed starter, not a complete atlas.
Temple practices and food concepts require tradition-specific human review.

items.description: Kerala Tourism describes Kumarakom toddy-shop culture, palm-sap collection, clay pots and regional food. Fresh sap is described as sweet; fermentation changes its character

items.title: Feni & urak heritage

items.title: Apong

items.title: Chhang
items.description: Incredible India describes Chhang as a Ladakhi barley-based beverage associated with festivals and celebrations. Regional fermented beverage

items.title: Sake-making traditions
items.description: UNESCO documents koji-based sake-making knowledge and its role in festivals, weddings and other social occasions. Craft knowledge; not one universal product specification

items.title: Agave & Tequila heritage
items.description: UNESCO describes the agave landscape and Tequila facilities as a cultural landscape connecting cultivation and production history. Landscape, agriculture and craft heritage

items.title: Bavarian festival culture
items.description: The official Oktoberfest history traces its origin to royal-wedding celebrations and a horse race in 1810. Festival history rather than a tasting recommendation

items.title: Lemon & cumin chana
items.description: Crisp cucumber, soft chickpeas, citrus finish. Unsweetened lime water
steps: Cook chickpeas until tender, or rinse ready-cooked chickpeas.
Wash and chop the vegetables using clean equipment.
Combine with lemon and cumin; keep added salt modest.
Serve promptly; chill leftovers promptly.

items.title: Roasted peanut koshimbir
items.description: Crunch with a fresh citrus contrast. Plain sparkling water
steps: Wash and chop cucumber and coriander.
Add a small portion of unsalted roasted peanuts.
Dress with lemon; do not add sweet bottled dressing by default.
Check nut allergies and cross-contact before serving.

items.title: Cooked moong chaat
items.description: Soft beans with bright herbs and acidity. Mint water
steps: Cook moong beans thoroughly rather than serving raw sprouts.
Wash and chop vegetables separately from raw animal foods.
Mix with herbs and lemon; add chilli to preference.
Serve fresh and refrigerate leftovers promptly.

items.title: Chickpea sundal bowl
items.description: Warm spice, gentle sweetness, tender pulses. Plain water
steps: Use fully cooked chickpeas.
Warm curry leaves and cumin in a small amount of oil.
Toss with chickpeas and a little coconut.
Check every ingredient and keep cooked food at safe serving temperatures.

items.title: Pepper & lime tofu bites
items.description: Peppery, citrus-led, soft with browned edges. Unsweetened iced tea
steps: Check the tofu label and soy allergy suitability.
Cut tofu and washed peppers into bite-sized pieces.
Bake or pan-cook with a little oil until thoroughly heated.
Finish with lime and pepper; serve with vegetables.

items.title: Herbed paneer & peppers
items.description: Creamy texture with herbs and citrus. Cucumber water
steps: Check milk allergy suitability and refrigeration.
Cut paneer and washed peppers.
Cook with a little oil and the spices until thoroughly heated.
Finish with fresh herbs; include vegetables rather than only cheese.

items.title: Banana-leaf fish plate
items.description: Gentle aromatics, flaky texture, lime finish. Plain water
steps: Use safely sourced fish and keep it chilled before cooking.
Prepare separately from ready-to-eat vegetables.
Wrap with ginger and cook until fish reaches a verified safe internal temperature using local food-safety guidance.
Check bones and serve with cooked vegetables.

items.title: Roasted vegetable crunch
items.description: Roasted sweetness, crisp edges, gentle spice. Unsweetened lemon water
steps: Wash the vegetables and use clean utensils.
Cut into even pieces and coat lightly with oil and cumin.
Roast until cooked; adjust texture for the diner.
Finish with lemon and serve without a heavy salty sauce.
